title: The AI Security family: AI Access Security, AI Guard (AI Guardrails), AI Red Teaming and the AI asset inventory

prose.text: Zscaler groups its AI products into one family. This subject says which part of the family answers which question before an answer goes deep.

prose.label: AI Access Security.
prose.text: {{access-security-capabilities}} The policy mechanics behind it are ZIA's: AI and ML rules in Cloud App Control, [[zia.cloud-app-control.ai-ml-rules]], prompt DLP in [[zia.dlp]], AI URL categories in [[zia.url-filtering]], decryption in [[zia.ssl-inspection]], and isolation in [[zbi.policy]].

prose.label: APIs.
prose.text: {{api-families}} The OneAPI base paths are in [[shared.oneapi.base-urls:base-path-table]]. The AI Infrastructure inventory and its paging rules are in [[ai-security.asset-inventory-api]]; AI Guard has its own API, in [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api]] and [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api]].

prose.label: AI Red Teaming.
prose.text: {{red-teaming-api}} What the captures do not settle about it is open {{gap:red-teaming-boundary}}.

prose.label: Not captured.
prose.text: Packaging, licensing and per-call accounting are open {{gap:packaging}}. Hooks into other products are mapped in [[shared.integrations]].

checks.do: Which part of the family the question is about: users' access to public AI apps (ZIA Cloud App Control, DLP, URL Filtering), runtime guardrails on prompts and responses (AI Guard), testing of an organization's own AI apps (AI Red Teaming), or the AI asset and issue inventory (AI Infrastructure API).
Whether the tenant is entitled to the product before treating a page or an API operation as available; no capture settles entitlement.

four-capabilities.statement: Zscaler's AI Security product page names four capabilities: AI Asset Management (finding shadow AI applications, mapping AI models and development tools, assessing posture across applications, infrastructure and data pipelines); Secure Access to AI Apps (warn, block or isolate access controls, data protection policies, content moderation); Secure AI Apps and Infrastructure (automated vulnerability testing with 25+ prebuilt probes, custom risk scanning, remediation guidance with progress tracking); and AI Governance (real-time compliance monitoring, alignment with regulatory frameworks, audit reporting).

quotes: AI Asset Management
Identifies shadow AI applications, maps AI models and development tools, and assesses security posture across applications, infrastructure, and data pipelines.
Secure Access to AI Apps
Manages user access through access controls (warn/block/isolate), enforces data protection policies, and implements content moderation for safe AI utilization.
Secure AI Apps and Infrastructure
Conducts automated vulnerability testing using 25+ prebuilt probes across risk categories.
Enables custom risk scanning and provides actionable remediation guidance with progress tracking.
AI Governance
Ensures real-time compliance monitoring, alignment with regulatory frameworks, and comprehensive audit reporting for governance and risk management.

sub-products.statement: The same page lists AI Red Teaming (automated vulnerability assessment and simulated attacks) and AI Guardrails (runtime protection against prompt injection and data poisoning) as separate supporting sub-products.

quotes: AI Red Teaming: Automated vulnerability assessment and simulated attack simulation
AI Guardrails: Runtime protection blocking prompt injections and data poisoning

access-security-capabilities.statement: Zscaler's AI Access Security page positions it for controlling access and content across public generative-AI applications, AI embedded in SaaS, AI agents and developer tools: discovery and classification of AI applications with usage reporting, prompt and response extraction and classification, user- and group-based allow, block, coach or warn and browser isolation controls, inline DLP on prompts with more than 100 dictionaries, moderation of prompts and responses, and inline controls for AI IDEs and developer tools.

quotes: Zscaler positions AI Access Security as the surface for controlling access and content across public generative-AI applications, AI embedded in SaaS, AI agents, and developer tools.
Discovers and classifies AI applications, including AI embedded in SaaS, and reports usage by users, departments, application trends, and at-risk data.
Provides prompt and response extraction, classification, and usage insight.
Applies user- and group-based access controls, including allow, block, coach or warn, and browser isolation with copy/paste controls.
Applies inline DLP to prompts using more than 100 dictionaries, with examples including source code, PII, PCI, and PHI.
Moderates prompts and responses for off-topic, restricted, toxic, or competitor-related content.
Applies inline controls to AI IDEs and developer tools that access AI data and infrastructure.

guardrails-page-is-ai-guard.statement: Zscaler's AI Guardrails product page describes Zscaler AI Guard: an inline inspection platform for AI applications and infrastructure, with guardrails for prompt injection, jailbreak, malicious URL, unreachable URL and invisible text, data protection that leverages 100+ predefined dictionaries and integrates AI channels into existing data loss prevention programs, moderation of toxic or competitive output, dashboards that show the prompts sent to models, track violations and test policies, and support for regulatory frameworks.

quotes: Zscaler AI Guard represents the company's inline inspection platform designed to protect artificial intelligence applications and infrastructure.
inline AI guardrails for prompt injection, jailbreak, malicious URL, unreachable URL, and invisible text
leverage 100+ predefined dictionaries
integrate AI channels into existing data loss prevention programs
monitor and prevent toxic or competitive outputs that have the potential to harm your brand
The platform provides dashboards enabling organizations to
see all prompts sent to your models, track policy violations, and test policies to understand how prompts will trigger
Guardrails help maintain alignment with regulatory frameworks and governance requirements for AI deployment.

guardrails-no-separate-surface.statement: AI Guardrails is a product-page name for AI Guard, not a separate configurable product: no Help tree or API carries the AI Guardrails name.
guardrails-no-separate-surface.conditions: Rests on the AI Guardrails page describing AI Guard (guardrails-page-is-ai-guard) and on a search of vendor/zscaler-help and the captured API specifications, which finds no AI Guardrails article tree or API. The AI Security API's guardrail resources are discovered cloud guardrail configurations (AWS Bedrock and Azure), an inventory item, not AI Guard policy.

api-families.statement: The captured AI Security API specification combines two families: AI Infrastructure, 17 operations served from `https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/aispm`, and AI Red Teaming, 97 operations served from `https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/airt`.

expect.description: API Reference Guide for AI Infrastructure
API Reference Guide for AI Red Teaming

red-teaming-api.statement: AI Red Teaming is the testing side of the family and AI Guard the runtime side: the product page describes Red Teaming as automated vulnerability assessment with prebuilt probes, and its 97 API operations (AI apps and integration tests, probes, test runs, scheduled tests, reports, remediation) are generated in the aisec surface.
red-teaming-api.conditions: Combines the product page (four-capabilities, sub-products) with the operation list in the captured specification, which `node scripts/kb.mjs surface aisec` prints; no captured Help article documents Red Teaming.

packaging.title: Licensing, SKUs and per-call accounting for AI Guard and the AI Security family
packaging.detail: Unverified legacy statement: AI Guard appears separately licensed, but the SKU and tier mapping is not captured; how inline inspection is billed (per call, per token, flat rate per seat) is not captured. The ZIA integration lists an AI Guard subscription as a prerequisite (ai-security.ai-guard.zia-integration:prerequisites); nothing else states packaging.
packaging.blocks: licensing, entitlement and cost answers for any AI Security product

red-teaming-boundary.title: Red Teaming entitlement, authentication scopes, live acceptance and its link to AI Guard
red-teaming-boundary.detail: Unverified legacy statement: static request and response schemas are captured for the 97 Red Teaming operations, but tenant entitlement, authentication scopes, live endpoint acceptance, and whether Red Teaming remediation or policy-generation output can be applied to AI Guard automatically are unverified.
red-teaming-boundary.blocks: whether Red Teaming can be automated against a tenant and whether its findings configure AI Guard
